solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Not against roughing up an opponent

indicators.note: roughing up means handling violently, so these letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they are not against beating up a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughing up' rearranges the ten letters of NOT AGAINST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival who contends against you is your adversary, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Identifying word as no French one

parts.note: taken as written
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A grammar point about the French word for no.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming word in grammar, one that identifies a person, place or thing, is this part of speech.

clue.text: Some British submarines set up and spring a trap

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters read upwards, so the run is reversed
some of the letters of the phrase are taken out of its middle

explanation.surface: Part of the navy's submarine fleet is deployed to catch an enemy unawares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks HSUBMA from britiSH SUBMArines and 'set up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait and attack by surprise is exactly to spring a trap on someone.

clue.text: Ended series, having exceeded time allowed

parts.note: something finished is over
a run is a series, as of wins or performances

explanation.surface: A TV series finished late after going past its slot.
explanation.definitionFit: To go past a set limit, especially of time, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: I am taking mother up to Muslim leader

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes the second into itself

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they are bringing their mother along to meet a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts M inside I AM, between the I and the AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The cleric who leads prayers in a mosque is called by this title.

clue.text: Thomas's initial motive for betrayal

indicators.note: initial points to the first letter of the word beside it

parts.note: a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: An inquiry into why a man called Thomas betrayed his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the crime of high treachery, a close synonym.

clue.text: Not a starter in the ocean race

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
a race is run over a course

explanation.surface: An unseeded yachtsman entering an ocean race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a sportsman, but here it is the first dish of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: At dinner the principal dish follows the starter, so it is the dish that is not one.

clue.text: Dead bodies seen in protected areas for shooting?

parts.note: a dead body is cold
frames are bodies, as in a large frame

explanation.surface: Corpses turn up on a private shooting estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it means young plants putting out shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass-topped garden boxes protect young seedlings as their shoots grow.

clue.text: Ring Henry, love

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone telephones Henry, calling him love.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle of light round a saint's head or the moon is this ring.

clue.text: Mixes drink for fund-raiser

parts.note: to jumble is to mix up
ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A bartender mixes drinks to raise money for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of donated second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale of donated bric-a-brac is held to raise money for a cause.

clue.text: Made up for having date wrong on the inside

indicators.note: the inside means the next word goes within the jumbled letters
wrong means the letters of the word are set in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: Someone apologised for getting the date mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the date's letters to ATED; the anagram is split around the inserted word, which the parse leaves to the answer. 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to expiate it, the same as compensating for it.

clue.text: Have a cigarette and look happier

definitions.meaning: to ignite a cigarette and start smoking

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to start smoking and to brighten in expression.

clue.text: A poor reason for limping?

parts.note: a feeble justification, read literally as the explanation a lame person gives for walking badly

explanation.surface: Someone offers a weak excuse for hobbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, unconvincing justification is a stock phrase built on lame meaning feeble and crippled.

clue.text: He won't get the sack if the bag's big enough

definitions.text: He won't get the sack if the bag's big enough

parts.words: He won't get the sack if the bag's big enough
parts.note: a bag is the tally of game shot, so the estate worker in charge of the birds keeps his job when the shoot goes well

explanation.surface: An employee is safe from dismissal provided enough is carried home.
explanation.definitionFit: The estate employee who rears game birds is judged by the size of the day's bag.

clue.text: Courses for non-drivers?

parts.note: routes for pedestrians, not driving lessons or golf courses for people who cannot hit off the tee

explanation.surface: Classes for people who cannot drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Footways are courses taken by walkers rather than motorists.

clue.text: Sort of map to study on journey

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: Reading a map while on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing relief by lines joining points of equal height is a kind of map.

clue.text: Move stealthily like Red Indian, quietly

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people (the clue uses a dated term)
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Sneaking up silently like a scout in an old western.
explanation.definitionFit: To go slowly and silently to avoid notice is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Scot returns to service somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: returns means the name is read back to front

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A Scotsman goes back to the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns IAN into NAI. Nairn is a town on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of this name lies on the Moray Firth in northern Scotland.

clue.text: Unspeakable acting!

parts.note: reads as dreadful performing, but means performing without words

explanation.surface: A critic damns a terrible performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent theatre conveyed by gesture alone is acting that is literally without speech.

clue.text: It's bad form not to

indicators.note: bad means the word is written badly, its letters out of order

explanation.surface: An etiquette ruling that refusing is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad form' looks like an idiom for poor manners, but 'bad' rearranges FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition is the opposite of to, marking a starting point rather than a destination.

clue.text: Being the boss I may interrupt cook

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: The boss barges into the kitchen to interrupt the cook.
explanation.definitionFit: The head or leader of a group is a straight synonym for the person in charge.

clue.text: It's smoked chestnuts and hazelnut

parts.note: old chestnuts are stale jokes, and corn is trite humour
a cob is a hazelnut, the cobnut

explanation.surface: A list of things smoked or roasted, nuts among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnuts' looks like a nut but means old jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe with a bowl made from a dried maize cob is smoked.

clue.text: Natural cover in Eden?

parts.note: the leaves Adam and Eve used to cover their nakedness in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: Wondering what plants grew in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam and Eve sewed leaves of a fruit tree to clothe themselves.

clue.text: Snow shoe accepted by some backward Arctic people

indicators.note: accepted by means the first piece is taken in by the second
backward means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a ski is a long runner worn to travel over snow

explanation.surface: Some northern people take up a snow shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' gives EMOS; 'accepted by' places the snow shoe after its first letter. The surface's 'Snow shoe' reads as one item of kit, not a ski.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous peoples of the far north, now usually called Inuit, an older collective name.

clue.text: Tool for portions of lobster?

definitions.meaning: the claws of a lobster, not servings of it

explanation.surface: A request for an implement to deal with pieces of lobster.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gripping implement and a crustacean's claws.

clue.text: Tart and explicit Rice/Webber piece

indicators.note: piece means a part of the words beside it is taken

explanation.surface: A frank, sharp review of a Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' takes the run in expliCIT RICe. Rice and Webber wrote musicals together.
explanation.definitionFit: The acid of lemons gives a sour, sharp taste, so it means tart.

clue.text: Islander comes out of trance

indicators.note: comes out of means the letters emerge from the word in a new order

explanation.surface: An island dweller wakes from a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Crete, the largest Greek island, is so called.

clue.text: Things cracked up to stupefy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: nuts are things you crack open

explanation.surface: Someone is dazed after things go to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' looks like an idiom for going mad, but 'up' reverses NUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or shock someone into insensibility is a direct synonym.

clue.text: The Hispano-French girl?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
la is the French word for the, carried over from The

explanation.surface: Asking about a girl of mixed Spanish and French background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is understood with both languages: Spanish EL then French LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, used here as an example, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Hardcastle is converted in religious places

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Hardcastle undergoes a religious conversion in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Large principal churches of dioceses are places of worship.

clue.text: Tread the stage

definitions.meaning: the flat part of a stair you put your foot on

explanation.surface: An actor walks onto the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stair tread and a stage in a process.

clue.text: Helpful belief I can spread around

indicators.note: spread around means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A conviction that does good when shared widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advantageous or good for you is a straight synonym.
